To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
an ANN model resulted in a better agreement between predicted and experimental data than RSM for the extraction of adenoine, cordycepins, and polysacchaides from O. sinensis CS119.

the ANN model is superior to RSP for predicting the extraction yields of adenosine (R2, RMSE = 0.995, and 0.022), cordycepin R2 = 0.934 and RMSE = 079, and polysacchride R2, RMSE=0.997, 0.18, respectively, from the Chinese caterpillar mushroom, Ophiocordeps sinensis.
the artificial neural network model was superior to the response surface methodology model and that the water extract exhibited better in vitro antioxidant and antibacterial activities.

the extraction and characterization of adenosine and cordyceps polysaccharides and their antioxidant and antibacterial properties.
the optimization of extraction conditions for adenosine and cordyceps from O. sinensis CS119, and the evaluation of the antioxidant and antibacterial activities of the water extract.
the optimization of the extraction process for adenosine and cordyceps using ANN and RSM, and the evaluation of the antioxidant and antibacterial activities of the extract.
